title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description:
You are given an integer array nums. For each element, count how many elements to its right are strictly smaller than it.

Return an integer array counts where counts[i] is the number of positions j > i such that nums[j] < nums[i]. The counts must be returned in the original order of nums.

A naive quadratic scan works but is too slow for large inputs; an efficient solution answers prefix-frequency queries while scanning from right to left.

examples.explanation: To the right of 5 there are two smaller elements (2 and 1). To the right of 2 there is one smaller element (1). To the right of 6 there is one smaller element (1). To the right of 1 there are no smaller elements.
A single element has nothing to its right.
Neither element is strictly greater than the element to its right.

approach: Coordinate-compress the values into dense ranks so arbitrary integers map to contiguous positions without changing comparisons. Scan the array from right to left maintaining a Fenwick (binary indexed) tree over ranks that records which values have already been seen (all of which lie to the right of the current index). For each element, a prefix-sum query up to its rank minus one counts already-seen values that are strictly smaller, which becomes its answer; then insert the current rank. Reversing the collected answers restores original order. With n elements, compression and n tree operations run in O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
